chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Al-Husayn ibn Alwan from 'Amr ibn Khalid from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to fast in Sha'ban and the month of Ramadan, connecting them, and he would forbid the people from connecting them. And he would say: 'They are the two months of Allah, and they are expiation for what is before them and what is after them.'

key_terms.رَمَضَان: Ramadan (the ninth month of the Islamic lunar calendar, known for fasting)
key_terms.شَعْبَان: Sha'ban (the eighth month of the Islamic lunar calendar)
key_terms.كَفَّ: The two months of Allah (a title of honor for Sha'ban and Ramadan)
key_terms.لِمَا بَعْدَهُمَا: For what is after them (sins committed after fasting)
key_terms.لِمَا قَبْلَهُمَا: For what is before them (sins committed prior to fasting)
key_terms.يَصِلُهُمَا: Connecting them (referring to fasting continuously from the end of Sha'ban into Ramadan without breaking the fast)

ai.seo_question: Why did the Prophet fast in Sha'ban but forbid others from connecting it to Ramadan?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani highlights the Prophet's unique practice of fasting in Sha'ban to bridge the gap between the sacred months, distinguishing his voluntary devotion from the general prohibition on 'connecting' fasts without a break. It underscores the theological significance of Sha'ban as a month of expiation (kaffarah) for sins, a concept deeply rooted in Shia jurisprudence regarding the virtues of the month preceding Ramadan. The narration reflects the scholarly emphasis on following the Prophet's specific example in acts of worship that are not obligatory but carry immense spiritual reward.
